Then, in particular, ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$, so, by \Cref{P-convex}, ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$. Next, we show that if ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ then $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$. If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$, then it follows from ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$, \eqref{eq-sc1} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ that $\lambda {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$. Thus the supremum in the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}\})$ is over a superset of the set the supremum in the definition of $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$ is taken over, which shows $\operatorname{dens}'_k(\{{\mathfrak q}\}) \ge \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak q}'\})$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} it then follows that $$ 2^{4a}2^{-n} < \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}''\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\})\,. $$ Similarly, it follows from ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}'$, ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$ and \eqref{def-cnk} that $$ \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}'\}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$ Thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C1 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C1-convex

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'\le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C-convex} and the inclusion ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, which holds by definition \eqref{defcnkj}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we have that ${\mathfrak q} \le {\mathfrak q}'$ and $100 {\mathfrak q}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ imply $100 {\mathfrak q} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. So, by \eqref{defbfp}, $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$. Consequently, by \eqref{defcnkj} $$ 2^j \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}'')|\le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p}')| \le |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| < 2^{j+1}\,, $$ thus ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C2 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C2-convex

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, we have \begin{equation*} {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)\ . \end{equation*} Combined with \Cref{C1-convex}, it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. If ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$ the statement is trivially true, otherwise suppose that ${\mathfrak p}' \notin {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C2-def}, this implies that there exists $0 \le l' \le Z(n+1)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$. By the definition \eqref{eq-L1-def} of ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l')$, this implies that ${\mathfrak p}'$ is minimal with respect to $\le$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j) \setminus \bigcup_{l < l'} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$. Since ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$ and ${\mathfrak p}\in{\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$, a contradiction.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C3 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C3-convex

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \Cref{C2-convex} it follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} and \eqref{eq-L2-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we then have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C4 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C4-convex

nodes.statement: The proof is entirely analogous to \Cref{C2-convex}, substituting ${\mathfrak C}_4$ for ${\mathfrak C}_2$, ${\mathfrak C}_3$ for ${\mathfrak C}_1$ and ${\mathfrak p}'\le{\mathfrak p}''$ for ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C5 convex
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the collection ${\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$ is convex.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C5-convex

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$ with ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. Then ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$ by \eqref{defc5}, and thus by \Cref{C4-convex} ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$. It suffices to show that if ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_4(k,n,j)$ by contraposition; this is true by \eqref{eq-L4-def} and ${\mathfrak p}\le{\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: dens compare
nodes.statement: We have for every $k\ge 0$ and ${\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$ \begin{equation} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak P}')\le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak P}')\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: dens-compare

nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'$ and $\lambda\ge 2$ and ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))} \le \sup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k): \lambda {\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}''} \frac{\mu({E}_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}. \end{equation} Let such ${\mathfrak p}'$, $\lambda$, ${\mathfrak p}$ be given. It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$, that is, it satisfies \eqref{muhj1} and \eqref{muhj2}. We show \eqref{muhj1}. As ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak P}')$, there exists ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}'$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By assumption on ${\mathfrak P}'$, we have ${\mathfrak p}''\in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k-1} \mu(J). \end{equation} Then also ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$, which proves \eqref{muhj1} for ${\mathfrak p}$. We show \eqref{muhj2}. Assume to get a contradiction that there exists $J\in \mathcal{D}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset J$ and \begin{equation} \mu(G\cap J)>2^{-k} \mu(J). \end{equation} As $\lambda{\mathfrak p}'\lesssim \lambda{\mathfrak p}$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, and therefore ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\subset J$. This contradicts ${\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}'\subset {\mathfrak P}(k)$. This proves \eqref{muhj2} for ${\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C dens1
nodes.statement: For each set $\mathfrak{A} \subset \mathfrak{C}(k,n)$, we have $$ \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C-dens1

nodes.statement: We have by \Cref{dens-compare} that $\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A})$. Since $\mathfrak{A} \subset {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$, it follows from monotonicity of suprema and the definition \eqref{eq-densdef} that $ \operatorname{dens}_k'(\mathfrak{A}) \le \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n))\,. $ By \eqref{eq-densdef} and \eqref{def-cnk}, we have $$ \operatorname{dens}_k'({\mathfrak C}(k,n)) = \sup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)} \operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{4a}2^{-n+1}\,. $$
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: relation geometry
nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$, then ${\mathcal{I}}(u) = {\mathcal{I}}(u')$ and \begin{equation*} B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \neq \emptyset\ . \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: relation-geometry

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u}, {\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$. If ${\mathfrak u} = {\mathfrak u}'$ then the conclusion of the Lemma clearly holds. Else, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and $2 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and $10 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$. Using \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \eqref{eq-sc2} of \Cref{wiggle-order-3}, we deduce that \begin{equation} 100 {\mathfrak p}\lesssim 100 {\mathfrak u}\,, \qquad 100 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim 100{\mathfrak u}'\,. \end{equation} Now suppose that $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$. Then we have $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}) \cap \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}') = \emptyset$, by the definition \eqref{defbfp} of $\mathfrak{B}$ and the definition \eqref{wiggleorder} of $\lesssim$, but also $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}) \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$ and $\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}') \subset \mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})$, by \eqref{defbfp}, \eqref{wiggleorder} and \eqref{eq-Fefferman-trick0}. Hence, $$ |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak p})| \geq |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u})| + |\mathfrak{B}({\mathfrak u}')| \geq 2^{j} + 2^j = 2^{j+1}\,, $$ which contradicts ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$. Therefore we must have \begin{equation*} B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) \ne \emptyset\, . \end{equation*} It follows from $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and $10{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ are nested. Combining this with the conclusion of the last paragraph and definition \eqref{defunkj} of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, we obtain that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: equivalence relation
nodes.statement: For each $k,n,j$, the relation $\sim$ on ${\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ is an equivalence relation.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: equivalence-relation

nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: C6 forest
nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)=\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)}\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: C6-forest

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-C4-def} and \eqref{defc5}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_3(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{eq-L2-def} and \eqref{eq-C3-def}, there exists ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, that is, with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$. Then $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u})$ is clearly nonempty, so ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$. By the definition of ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}'$. By \eqref{definesv}, we have ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u}')$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: forest geometry
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ satisfies \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: forest-geometry

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{definesv}, there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. Then we have $2{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \ne {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$, so by \eqref{eq-sc3} $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$. Further, by \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and there exists ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100)$. Let ${\theta} \in B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1)$. Using the triangle inequality and the fact that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') ={\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, we obtain \begin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\theta}) &\le d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\ &= d_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\vartheta}) + d_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {\theta})\\ &< 100 + 100 + 1 < 500\,. \end{align*} Combining this with $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim 500{\mathfrak u}'$, we obtain $$ B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), 1) \subset B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 500) \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 4)\,. $$ Together with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$, this gives $4{\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$, which is \eqref{forest1}.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: forest convex
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$, the set $\mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ satisfies the convexity condition \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: forest-convex

nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$. By \eqref{definesv} we have ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{C5-convex}, we have ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$ we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) 
ot \subset G'$, so ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
ot \subset G'$ and therefore also ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \eqref{definesv} there exists ${\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence $2{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') 
e {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. Together this implies ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. With the inclusion ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ from ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}''$, it follows that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and hence ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
e {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$. By \eqref{eq-sc1} and transitivity of $\lesssim$ we further have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$, so ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$, which shows \eqref{forest2}.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: forest separation
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u},{\mathfrak u}'\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ we have \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) > 2^{Z(n+1)}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: forest-separation

nodes.statement:
By the definition \eqref{eq-C2-def} of ${\mathfrak C}_2(k,n,j)$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})- Z(n+1)$. By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} we have $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}')) \ge 2^{95a Z(n+1)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-sc1} we have $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim 2{\mathfrak p}$, so by transitivity of $\lesssim$ there exists $\mathfrak{v} \sim {\mathfrak u}$ with $2{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim \mathfrak{v}$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') 
e {\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{v})$. Since ${\mathfrak u}, {\mathfrak u}'$ are not equivalent under $\sim$, we have $\mathfrak{v} 
ot \sim {\mathfrak u}'$, thus $10{\mathfrak p}' 
ot\lesssim {\mathfrak u}'$. This implies that there exists $q \in B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 1) \setminus B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 10)$. From ${\mathfrak p}' \le {\mathfrak p}$, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} it then follows that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak p}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &\ge -d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) - d_{{\mathfrak u}'}(q, {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'))\ &> -1 + 10 - 1 = 8\,. \end{align*} The lemma follows by combining the two displays with the fact that $95 a \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: forest inner
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u}\in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$ we have \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: forest-inner

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})$. Then ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_4(k,n,j)$, hence there exists a chain $$ {\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}_{Z(n+1)} \le \dotsb \le {\mathfrak p}_0 $$ of distinct tiles in ${\mathfrak C}_3(n,k,j)$. We pick such a chain and set ${\mathfrak q} = {\mathfrak p}_0$. Then we have from distinctness of the tiles in the chain that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1)$. By \eqref{eq-C3-def} there exists ${\mathfrak u}'' \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$ with $2{\mathfrak q} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'')$. Then we have in particular by \Cref{wiggle-order-1} that $10 {\mathfrak p} \lesssim {\mathfrak u}''$. Let ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}$ be such that ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}')$. By the definition of $\sim$, it follows that ${\mathfrak u}' \sim {\mathfrak u}''$. By transitivity of $\sim$, we have ${\mathfrak u} \sim {\mathfrak u}''$. By \Cref{relation-geometry}, we have ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}'') = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$, hence ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) < {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak q}) - Z(n+1) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$. Thus, there exists some cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I) = {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak u}) - Z(n+1) - 1$ and $I \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset I$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j)$, we have that $I \notin \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak u})$, so $B(c(I), 8D^{s(I)}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By the triangle inequality, \eqref{defineD} and $a \ge 4$, the same then holds for the subcube ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset I$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: forest stacking
nodes.statement: It holds for $k\le n$ that \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le (4n+12)2^{n}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: forest-stacking

nodes.statement: Suppose that a point $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$. Since ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j) \subset {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for each such ${\mathfrak u}$, there exists $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. We fix such an $\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u}) := \mathfrak{m}$ for each ${\mathfrak u}$, and claim that the map ${\mathfrak u} \mapsto\mathfrak{m}({\mathfrak u})$ is injective. Indeed, assume for ${\mathfrak u}\neq {\mathfrak u}'$ there is $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ such that $100{\mathfrak u} \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$ and $100{\mathfrak u}' \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, either ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By \eqref{defunkj}, $B_{{\mathfrak u}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}),100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak u}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}'), 100) = \emptyset$. This contradicts $\Omega(\mathfrak{m})$ being contained in both sets by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}. Thus $x$ is contained in more than $(4n + 12)2^n$ cubes ${\mathcal{I}}(\mathfrak{m})$, $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$. Consequently, we have by \eqref{eq-Aoverlap-def} that $x \in A(2n + 6, k,n) \subset G_2$. Let ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ be an inclusion minimal cube among the ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}'), {\mathfrak u}' \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ with $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ for all cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}')$ containing $x$. Thus $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}) \subset \{y \ : \ \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}(y) > 1 + (4n+12)2^{n}\} \subset G_2\,. $$ Thus $\mathfrak{T}_1({\mathfrak u}) \cap {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \emptyset$. This contradicts ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_2(k,n,j)$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.statement: We first fix $k,n, j$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{defineep}, we have that $\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)$ and hence $\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G \setminus G'} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)= 0$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_5(k,n,j) \setminus {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. Thus it suffices to estimate the contribution of the sets ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$. By \Cref{forest-stacking}, we can decompose ${\mathfrak U}_3(k,n,j)$ as a disjoint union of at most $4n + 12$ collections ${\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)$, $1 \le l \le 4n+12$, each satisfying $$ \sum_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} \le 2^n\,. $$ By Lemmas \ref{forest-geometry}, \ref{forest-convex}, \ref{forest-separation}, \ref{forest-inner} and \ref{C-dens1}, the pairs $$ ({\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l), \mathfrak{T}_2|_{{\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)}) $$ are $n$-forests for each $k,n,j,l$, and by \Cref{C6-forest}, we have $$ {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) = \bigcup_{l = 1}^{4n + 12} \bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})\,. $$ Since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not\subset G_1$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j)$, we have ${\mathfrak C}_6(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} = \emptyset$ and hence $$ \operatorname{dens}_2(\bigcup_{{\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}_4(k,n,j,l)} \mathfrak{T}_2({\mathfrak u})) \le 2^{2a + 5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}\,. $$ Using the triangle inequality according to the splitting by $k,n,j$ and $l$ in \eqref{disclesssim1} and applying \Cref{forest-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate $$ \sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k} (2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{440a^3}2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}(2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2 \|\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 $$ for the left hand side of \eqref{disclesssim1}. Since $|f| \le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. We get a bound $$ 2^{440a^3} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{1 -\frac{1}{q}} 2^{2a+5}\sum_{k \ge 0}\sum_{n \ge k}(2n+3)(4n+12) 2^{-(1-\frac{1}{q})n}\,. $$ Interchanging the order of summation, the last factor equals $$ 2^{2a+5} \sum_{n \ge 0} (2n+3)(4n+12) (n+1) 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}\,. $$ Up to an explicit constant, the sum is bounded by $\sum n^3 2^{-\frac{q-1}{q}n}$, which is at most some constant times $1/(q-1)^4$ by comparing to an integral. Since $a \ge 4$, this is overall bounded by $2^{a^3}/(q-1)^4$, which completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: antichain decomposition
nodes.statement: We have that \begin{align} &\quad {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &= \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k} {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'} \\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\\ &\quad\cup \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \bigcup_{n \ge k}\bigcup_{0 \le j \le 2n+3} \bigcup_{0 \le l \le Z(n+1)} {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)\cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}\,. \end{align}
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: antichain-decomposition

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$. Clearly, for every cube $J = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$ there exists some $k \ge 0$ such that \eqref{muhj1} holds, and for no cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ and no $k < 0$ does \eqref{muhj2} hold. Thus ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ for some $k \ge 0$. Next, since $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')\cap G$ for every $\lambda \ge 2$ and every tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ with $\lambda{\mathfrak p} \lesssim \lambda {\mathfrak p}'$, it follows from \eqref{muhj2} that $\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}')) \le 2^{-k} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))$ for every such ${\mathfrak p}'$, so $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}\}) \le 2^{-k}$. Combining this with $a \ge 0$, it follows from \eqref{def-cnk} that there exists $n\ge k$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$. Since ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$, we have in particular ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset A(2n + 6, k, n)$, so there exist at most $1 + (4n + 12)2^n < 2^{2n+4}$ tiles $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le \mathfrak{m}$. It follows that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ or ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ for some $1 \le j \le 2n + 3$. In the former case we are done, in the latter case the equality to be shown follows from the definitions of the collections ${\mathfrak C}_i$ and ${\mathfrak L}_i$.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.name: L0 antichain
nodes.statement: We have that $$ {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n) = \dot{\bigcup_{0 \le l < n}} {\mathfrak L}_0(k,n,l)\,, $$ where each ${\mathfrak L}_0(k,n,l)$ is an antichain.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: L0-antichain

nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that ${\mathfrak L}_0(k,n)$ contains no chain of length $n + 1$. Suppose that we had such a chain ${\mathfrak p}_0 \le {\mathfrak p}_1 \le \dotsb \le {\mathfrak p}_{n}$ with ${\mathfrak p}_i 
e {\mathfrak p}_{i+1}$ for $i =0, \dotsc, n-1$. By \eqref{def-cnk}, we have that $\operatorname{dens}_k'(\{{\mathfrak p}_n\}) > 2^{-n}$. Thus, by \eqref{eq-densdef}, there exists ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ and $\lambda \ge 2$ with $\lambda {\mathfrak p}_n \le \lambda {\mathfrak p}'$ and  egin{equation}  rac{\mu(E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}'))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))} > \lambda^{a} 2^{4a} 2^{-n}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathfrak{O}$ be the set of all ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak P}(k)$ such that we have $ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda) \cap \Omega({\mathfrak p}'') 
eq \emptyset$. We now show that  egin{equation} |\mathfrak{O}| \le 2^{4a}\lambda^a\,. \end{equation} The balls $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)$, ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ are disjoint by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, and by the triangle inequality contained in $B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), \lambda+1.2)$. By assumption \eqref{thirddb} on $\Theta$, this ball can be covered with $$ 2^{a\lceil \log_2(\lambda+1.2) + \log_2(5)ceil} \le 2^{a(\log_2(\lambda) + 4)} = 2^{4a}\lambda^a $$ many $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}$-balls of radius $0.2$. Here we have used that for $\lambda \ge 2$ $$ \lceil \log_2(\lambda + 1.2) + \log_2(5) ceil \le 1+ \log_2(1.6 \lambda) + \log_2(5) = 4 + \log_2(\lambda)\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, each such ball contains at most one ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is contained in one of the balls. Thus we get \eqref{eq-O-bound}. By \eqref{definee1} and \eqref{definee2} we have $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset  igcup_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}} E_1({\mathfrak p}'')$, thus $$ 2^{4a}\lambda^a 2^{-n} < \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}}  rac{\mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}''))}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}''))}\,. $$ Hence there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}'' \in \mathfrak{O}$ with  egin{equation*} \mu(E_1({\mathfrak p}'')) \ge 2^{-n} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'))\,. \end{equation*} By the definition \eqref{mnkmax} of $\mathfrak{M}(k,n)$, there exists a tile $\mathfrak{m} \in \mathfrak{M}(k,n)$ with ${\mathfrak p}' \leq \mathfrak{m}$. From \eqref{eq-p'}, the inclusion $E_2(\lambda, {\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $a\ge 1$ we obtain $$ 2^n \geq 2^{4a} \lambda^{a} \geq \lambda\,. $$ From the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and $a \ge 1$, we now obtain for all ${\vartheta} \in B_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), 1)$ that  egin{align*} &\quad d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\vartheta})\ &\leq d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_0), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{n}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\ &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{{\mathfrak p}_0}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta})\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an} (d_{{\mathfrak p}_{n}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_n), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')) + d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''))\ &\quad+ d_{{\mathfrak p}''}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), {\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m})) + d_{\mathfrak{m}}({\mathcal{Q}}(\mathfrak{m}), {\vartheta}))\ &\leq 1 + 2^{-95an}(\lambda + (\lambda + 1) + 1 + 1) \leq 100\,. \end{align*} Thus, by \eqref{straightorder}, $100{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim \mathfrak{m}$, a contradiction to ${\mathfrak p}_0 
otin {\mathfrak C}(k,n)$.

nodes.name: L2 antichain
nodes.statement: Each of the sets ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is an antichain.

nodes.label: L2-antichain

nodes.statement:
Suppose that there are ${\mathfrak p}_0, {\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathfrak p}_0 
e {\mathfrak p}_1$ and ${\mathfrak p}_0 \le {\mathfrak p}_1$. By \Cref{wiggle-order-1} and \Cref{wiggle-order-2}, it follows that $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_1$. Since ${\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$ is finite, there exists a maximal $l \ge 1$ such that there exists a chain $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_1 \lesssim \dotsb \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l$ with all ${\mathfrak p}_i$ in ${\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ and ${\mathfrak p}_i 
e {\mathfrak p}_{i+1}$ for $i = 0, \dotsc, l-1$. If we have ${\mathfrak p}_l \in {\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, then it follows from $2{\mathfrak p}_0 \lesssim 200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim {\mathfrak p}_l$ and \eqref{eq-L2-def} that ${\mathfrak p}_0 
ot\in {\mathfrak L}_2(k,n,j)$, a contradiction. Thus, by the definition \eqref{defunkj} of ${\mathfrak U}_1(k,n,j)$, there exists ${\mathfrak p}_{l+1} \in {\mathfrak C}_1(k,n,j)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_l) \subsetneq {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}) $ and ${\vartheta} \in B_{{\mathfrak p}_l}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_l), 100) \cap B_{{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{l+1}), 100)$. Using the triangle inequality and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, one deduces that $200 {\mathfrak p}_l \lesssim 200{\mathfrak p}_{l+1}$. This contradicts maximality of $l$.

nodes.name: L1 L3 antichain
nodes.statement: Each of the sets ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$ and ${\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)$ is an antichain.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson
nodes.label: L1-L3-antichain

nodes.statement: By its definition \eqref{eq-L1-def}, each set ${\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of minimal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak L}_1(k,n,j,l)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak q}$, then ${\mathfrak q}$ would not be minimal. Hence such ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q}$ do not exist. Similarly, by \eqref{eq-L3-def}, each set ${\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)$ is a set of maximal elements in some set of tiles with respect to $\le$. If there were distinct ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak q} \in {\mathfrak L}_3(k,n,j,l)$ with ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak q}$, then ${\mathfrak p}$ would not be maximal.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of discrete Carleson

nodes.statement: If ${\mathfrak p} \not\in {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$, then $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap (G \setminus G')) = 0$. By \eqref{definetp} and \eqref{definee1}, it follows that $\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G \setminus G'} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = 0$ for almost every $x$. We thus have, almost everywhere, $$ \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x) = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}_2 \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}} T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(x)\,. $$ Let ${\mathfrak L}(k,n)$ denote any of the terms ${\mathfrak L}_i(k,n,j,l) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{eq-fp'-decomposition}, where the indices $j, l$ may be void. Then ${\mathfrak L}(k,n)$ is an antichain, by Lemmas \ref{L0-antichain},\ref{L2-antichain}, \ref{L1-L3-antichain}. Further, we have \begin{equation*} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak L}(k,n)) \le 2^{4a+1 - n} \end{equation*} by \Cref{C-dens1}, and we have \begin{equation*} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak L}(k,n)) \le 2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)}, \end{equation*} since \begin{equation*} {\mathfrak L}(k,n) \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F,G} \subset {\mathfrak P}_{G \setminus G'} \cap {\mathfrak P}_{F, G} = \emptyset. \end{equation*} Applying now the triangle inequality according to the decomposition coming from \Cref{antichain-decomposition}, and then applying \Cref{antichain-operator} to each term, we obtain the estimate \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} (n + (2n+4) + 2(2n+4) (1+Z(n+1))) \\ \times 2^{117a^3}(q-1)^{-1} (2^{4a+1-n})^{\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} (2^{2a+5} \frac{\mu(F)}{\mu(G)})^{\frac{1}{q} - \frac{1}{2}} \|f\|_2\|\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2\,. \end{multline*} Because $|f| \le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F$, we have $\|f\|_2 \le \mu(F)^{1/2}$, and we have $\|\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{G\setminus G'}\|_2 \le \mu(G)^{1/2}$. Using this and \eqref{defineZ}, we bound $$ \le 2^{118a^3} (q - 1)^{-1} \mu(F)^{\frac{1}{q}} \mu(G)^{\frac{1}{q'}} \sum_{k \ge 0} \sum_{n \ge k} n^2 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}}\,. $$ The last sum equals, by changing the order of summation, $$ \sum_{n \ge 0} n^2(n+1) 2^{-n\frac{q-1}{8a^4}} \le \frac{2^{2a^3}}{(q-1)^4}\,. $$ This completes the proof.

nodes.name: tile disjointness
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}$. If there exists an $x\in X$ with $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\cap E({\mathfrak p}')$, then ${\mathfrak p}= {\mathfrak p}'$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: tile-disjointness

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p},{\mathfrak p}'$ and $x$ be given. Assume without loss of generality that ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. As we have $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and $x\in E({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ by Definition \eqref{defineep}, we conclude for $i=1,2$ that ${Q}(x)\in{\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${Q}(x)\in{\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. By \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic} we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')\subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$. By Definition \eqref{straightorder}, we conclude ${\mathfrak p}\le {\mathfrak p}'$. As $\mathfrak{A}$ is an antichain, we conclude ${\mathfrak p}={\mathfrak p}'$. This proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: maximal bound antichain
nodes.statement: Let $x\in X$. Then \begin{equation} | \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}}T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)|\le 2^{102 a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}} f (x) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: maximal-bound-antichain

nodes.statement: Fix $x\in X$. By \Cref{tile-disjointness}, there is at most one ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}$ such that $T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)$ is not zero. If there is no such ${\mathfrak p}$, the estimate \eqref{hlmbound} follows. Assume there is such a ${\mathfrak p}$. By definition of $T_{{\mathfrak p}}$ we have $x\in E({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x, {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} Let $y\in X$ with $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)\neq 0$. By Definition \eqref{defks} of $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ we have \begin{equation} \frac{1}{4} D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})-1} \leq \rho(x,y) \leq \frac{1}{2} D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} The triangle inequality with \eqref{eqtttt0} and \eqref{supp-Ks1} implies \begin{equation} \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),y) < 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} Using the kernel bound \eqref{eqkernel-size} and the lower bound in \eqref{supp-Ks} we obtain \begin{equation} |K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)|\le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x,\frac 14 D^{{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}-1}))}\, . \end{equation} Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $5 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{5a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x, 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\, \end{equation} which, thanks to the closeness of the points $x$ and ${\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})$ shown in \eqref{eqtttt0}, is in turn bounded by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{6a+101a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\, . \end{equation} Using that {$|e({\vartheta})|$} is bounded by $1$ for every ${\vartheta}\in {\Theta}$, we estimate with the triangle inequality and the above information \begin{equation} | T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)| \le \frac{2^{6a+101 a^3}}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} \int _{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} |f(y)|\, dy \end{equation} This together with $a\ge 4$ proves the Lemma.

nodes.statement: We have that \begin{equation} \left|\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)\, d\mu(x)\right|\le 2^{103a^3}({q}-1)^{-1} \operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \|f\|_2\|g\|_2\, . \end{equation}

nodes.label: dens2-antichain

nodes.statement: We have $f=\bm{\mathrm{1}}_Ff$. Using H\"older's inequality, we obtain for each $x\in B'$ and each $B'\in \mathcal{B}$ using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} |f(y)|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3\tilde{q}-2}}\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \left(\frac 1{\mu(B')}\int_{B'} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F(y)\, d\mu(y)\right)^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left(M_{\mathcal{B}} (|f|^{\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}})(x)\right)^{\frac 32-\frac 1{\tilde{q}}} \operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} Taking the maximum over all $B'$ containing $x$, we obtain \begin{equation} M_{\mathcal{B}}|f|\le M_{\mathcal{B},\frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2} } |f| \operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12}\, . \end{equation} We have with \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood} \begin{equation} \left\|M_{\mathcal{B}, \frac {2{\tilde{q}}}{3{\tilde{q}}-2}} f\right\|_2\le 2^{2a}(3\tilde{q}-2)(2\tilde{q}-2)^{-1}\|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} Using $1<\tilde{q}\le 2$ estimates the last display by \begin{equation} 2^{2a+2} (\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|f\|_2\, . \end{equation} We obtain with Cauchy-Schwarz and then \Cref{maximal-bound-antichain} \begin{equation} |\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)\, d\mu(x)| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \|g\|_2 \Big\| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \Big\|_2 \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3}\|g\|_2 \| M_{\mathcal{B}}f \|_2 \end{equation} With \eqref{eqttt1} and \eqref{eqttt2} we can estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{102a^3+2a+2}(\tilde{q}-1)^{-1} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{\tilde{q}}-\frac 12} \end{equation} Using $a\ge 4$ and $(\tilde q - 1)^{-1} = (q+1)/(q-1) \le 3(q-1)^{-1}$ proves the lemma.

nodes.statement: We write for the expression inside the absolute values on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqttt3} \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}}\iint \overline{g(x)} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x) {K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)}e({Q}(x)(y) - {Q}(x)(x)) f(y)\, d\mu(y)\,d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} \overline{T_{{\mathfrak p}} ^*g(y)} f(y)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with the adjoint operator \begin{equation} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^*g(y)=\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)}e(-{Q}(x)(y)+ {Q}(x)(x))g(x)\, d\mu(x)\, . \end{equation} We have by expanding the square \begin{equation} \int \Big|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}}T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\Big|^2\, d\mu(y)= \int \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\right) \left(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}}\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\right)\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}} \Big|\int T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} We split the sum into the terms with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Using the symmetry of each summand, we may switch ${\mathfrak p}$ and ${\mathfrak p}'$ in the second sum. Using further positivity of each summand to replace the condition ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ by ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ in the second sum, we estimate \eqref{eqtts1} by \begin{equation} \le2 \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}: {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \Big|\int T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)}\, d\mu(y)\Big|\,. \end{equation} Define for ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}$ \begin{equation} B({\mathfrak p}):=B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \end{equation} and define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p}):=\{{\mathfrak p}'\in\mathfrak{A}: {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')\leq {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) \land {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B({\mathfrak p})\}. \end{equation} Note that by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} applied $6$ times we have \begin{equation} \mu(B({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{6a} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))\, . \end{equation} Using \Cref{tile-correlation} and \eqref{eqttt4}, we estimate \eqref{eqtts2} by \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+6a+1} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g|(y) h({\mathfrak p})\, d\mu(y) \end{equation} with $h({\mathfrak p})$ defined as \begin{equation} \frac 1{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))}\int \sum_{{\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p})} {(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}}(\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p}')}|g|)(y')\, d\mu(y')\,. \end{equation} Note that $p>4$ since $a\ge 4$. Let $p'$ be the dual exponent of $p$, satisfying $1/p+1/p'=1$. We estimate $h({\mathfrak p})$ as defined in \eqref{def-hp} with H\"older using $|g|\le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_G$ and $E({\mathfrak p}')\subset B({\mathfrak p})$ by \begin{equation} \frac{\|g\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{B({\mathfrak p})}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))} \Big\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}({\mathfrak p})}(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_G\Big\|_{p}\, . \end{equation} Then we apply \Cref{antichain-tile-count} to estimate this by \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a} \frac{\|g\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{B({\mathfrak p})}\|_{p'}}{\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu(B({\mathfrak p}))^{\frac 1p}\,. \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{B}'$ be the collection of all balls $B({\mathfrak p})$

nodes.name: tile correlation
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({{\mathfrak p}'})\leq {\mathrm{s}}({{\mathfrak p}})$. Then \begin{equation} \left|\int T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g}\right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3}\frac{(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}}{\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))}\int_{E({\mathfrak p}')}|g|\int_{E({\mathfrak p})}|g|\,. \end{equation} Moreover, the term \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} vanishes unless \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation}

For every ${\vartheta}\in{\Theta}$ and every antichain $\mathfrak{A}$ we have \begin{equation} \Big\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}(1+d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\vartheta}))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_G\Big\|_{p} \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{5a}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}\right)^{\frac 1p}\, . \end{equation}

nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} \left(\frac 1{\tilde{q}} -\frac 12\right) (2-q)= \frac 1q -\frac 12\,. \end{equation} Multiplying the $(2-q)$-th power of \eqref{eqttt9} and the $(q-1)$-th power of \eqref{eqttt3} and estimating gives after simplification of some factors \begin{equation} \Big|\int \overline{g(x)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(x)\, d\mu(x)\Big| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{117a^3}(q-1)^{-1} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac {q-1}{2p}}\operatorname{dens}_2(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1{q}-\frac 12} \|f\|_2\|g\|_2\, . \end{equation} With the definition of $p$, this implies \Cref{antichain-operator}.

nodes.name: correlation kernel bound
nodes.statement: Let $-S\le s_1\le s_2\le S$ and let $x_1,x_2\in X$. Define \begin{equation} \varphi(y) := \overline{K_{s_1}(x_1, y)} K_{s_2}(x_2, y) \, . \end{equation} If $\varphi(y)\neq 0$, then \begin{equation} y\in B(x_1, D^{s_1})\, . \end{equation} Moreover, we have with $\tau = 1/a$ \begin{equation} \|\varphi\|_{C^\tau(B(x_1, 2 D^{s_1}))}\le \frac{2^{231 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: correlation-kernel-bound

nodes.statement: If $\varphi(y)$ is not zero, then $K_{s_1}(x_1, y)$ is not zero and thus \eqref{supp-Ks} gives \eqref{eqt10}. We next have for $y$ with \eqref{eq-Ks-size} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)|\le \frac{2^{204 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \end{equation} and for $y'\neq y$ additionally with \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} \begin{equation} |\varphi(y)-\varphi(y')| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le |K_{s_1}(x_1,y)-K_{s_1}(x_1,y'))|| K_{s_2}(x_2, y)| \end{equation} \begin{equation}+|K_{s_1}(x_1, y')| |K_{s_2}(x_2, y) - K_{s_2}(x_2, y'))| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{229 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}+ \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_2}}\right)^{1/a}\right) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{230 a^3}}{\mu(B(x_1, D^{s_1}))\mu(B(x_2, D^{s_2}))} \left(\frac{ \rho(y,y')}{D^{s_1}}\right)^{1/a}\,. \end{equation} Adding the estimates \eqref{suppart} and \eqref{holderpart} gives \eqref{eqt11}. This proves the lemma.
