nodes.name: tile range support
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak P}$, and each $y\in X$, we have that \begin{equation} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(y)\neq 0 \end{equation} implies \begin{equation} y\in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: tile-range-support

nodes.statement: Fix ${\mathfrak p}$ and $y$ with \eqref{tstargnot0}. Then there exists $x\in E({\mathfrak p})$ with \begin{equation} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)}e(-{Q}(x)(y) +{Q}(x)(x))g(x) \neq 0\, . \end{equation} As $E({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ and by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have \begin{equation} \rho(x,{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) < 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} As $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x,y)\neq 0$, we have by \eqref{supp-Ks} that \begin{equation} \rho(x,y)\le \frac 12 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} Now \eqref{ynotfar} follows by the triangle inequality.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}_1, {\mathfrak p}_2\in {\mathfrak P}$ with $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_1),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)}) \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_2),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_2)}) \ne \emptyset$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({{\mathfrak p}_1})\leq {\mathrm{s}}({{\mathfrak p}_2})$. For each $x_1\in E({\mathfrak p}_1)$ and $x_2\in E({\mathfrak p}_2)$ we have \begin{equation} 1+d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2))\le 2^{8a}(1 + d_{B(x_1, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})}({Q}(x_1),{Q}(x_2)))\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: tile-uncertainty

nodes.statement: Let $i\in \{1,2\}$. By Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have ${Q}(x_i)\in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}_i)$ With \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we then conclude \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}_i}({Q}(x_i),{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_i)) < 1\, . \end{equation} We have by the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_2),14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_2)})$. Thus, using again \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({Q}(x_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2)) \le 2^{6a} d_{{\mathfrak p}_2}({Q}(x_2), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2)) \le 2^{6a}\,. \end{equation} By the triangle inequality, we obtain from \eqref{dponetwo} and \eqref{tgeo0.5} \begin{equation} 1+d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_2))\le 2 + 2^{6a} +d_{{\mathfrak p}_1}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} As $x_1\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1)$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} d(x_1,{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_1))\le 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_1)\subset B(x_1,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})\, . \end{equation} We thus estimate the right-hand side of \eqref{tgeo1} with monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of the metrics $d_B$ by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} + d_{B(x_1,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} This is further estimated by applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} three times by \begin{equation} \le 2 + 2^{6a} +2^{3a}d_{B_1(x_1, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_1)})}({Q}(x_1), {Q}(x_2))\, . \end{equation} Now \eqref{tgeo} follows with $a\ge 4$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.statement: We begin with \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. By Lemma \ref{tile-range-support}, the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} vanishes if $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) = \emptyset$. Thus we can assume for the remainder of the proof that \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \neq \emptyset\,. \end{equation} We expand the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} as \begin{equation} \left|\int \int_{E({\mathfrak p}')} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}(x_1,y)}e(-{Q}(x_1)(y)+ {Q}(x_1)(x_1))g(x_1)\, d\mu(x_1) \right. \end{equation} \begin{equation} \times \left.\int_{E({\mathfrak p})} {K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(x_2,y)}e({Q}(x_2)(y) -{Q}(x_2)(x_2))\overline{g(x_2)}\, d\mu(x_2)\, d\mu(y)\right|\, . \end{equation} By Fubini and the triangle inequality and the fact $|e({Q}(x_i)(x_i))|=1$ for $i=1,2$, we can estimate \eqref{tstartstar} and \eqref{tstartstar'} from above by \begin{equation} \int_{E({\mathfrak p}')} \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2)\, d\mu(x_1)d\mu(x_2)\,. \end{equation} with \begin{equation} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2):= \left|\int e(-{Q}(x_1)(y)+{Q}(x_2)(y))\varphi_{x_1,x_2}(y) d\mu(y) \, g(x_1)g(x_2)\right| \end{equation} We estimate for fixed $x_1\in E({\mathfrak p}')$ and $x_2\in E({\mathfrak p})$ the inner integral of \eqref{eqa1} with \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput}. The function $\varphi:=\varphi_{x_1,x_2}$ satisfies the assumptions of \Cref{Holder-van-der-Corput} with $z = x_1$ and $R = D^{s_1}$ by \Cref{correlation-kernel-bound}. We obtain with $B':= B(x_1, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})$, \begin{equation*} {\bf I}(x_1, x_2) \le 2^{8a} \mu(B') \|{\varphi}\|_{C^\tau(B')} (1 + d_{B'}({Q}(x_1),{Q}(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)| \end{equation*} \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3+8a}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} (1 + d_{B'}({Q}(x_1),{Q}(x_2)))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}\,. \end{equation} Using \eqref{intersec5B}, \Cref{tile-uncertainty} and $a\ge 1$ estimates \eqref{eqa1.5} by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{231a^3 + 8a + 1}} {\mu(B(x_2, D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))} (1+d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p})))^{-1/(2a^2+a^3)}|g(x_1)g(x_2)|\,. \end{equation} As $x_2\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ by Definition \eqref{defineep} of $E$, we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} \rho(x_2,{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})) < 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} \end{equation} and thus by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} again and the triangle inequality \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset B(x_2,8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation} Using three iterations of the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} give \begin{equation} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{3a}\mu(B(x_2,D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))\, . \end{equation} With $a\ge 4$ and \eqref{eqa2} we conclude \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est}. Now assume the left-hand side of \eqref{eq-basic-TT*-est} is not zero. There is a $y\in X$ with \begin{equation} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}'}g(y)\overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}}g(y)}\neq 0 \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \Cref{tile-range-support}, we conclude \begin{equation} \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),{\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'))\le \rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),y) +\rho({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),y) \le 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}+5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}\le 10 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\, . \end{equation} By the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, we conclude \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 14D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation} This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{tile-correlation}.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: tile reach
nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta}\in {\Theta}$ and $N\ge0$ be an integer. Let ${\mathfrak p}, {\mathfrak p}'\in {\mathfrak P}$ with \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\vartheta}))\le 2^N\, \end{equation} \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\vartheta}))\le 2^N\, . \end{equation} Assume ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Then \begin{equation}2^{N+2}{\mathfrak p}\lesssim 2^{N+2} {\mathfrak p}'\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: tile-reach

nodes.statement: By \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we have \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}) \le 2^{N} \, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{eqassumedismfa} and the triangle inequality, we obtain \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{N+1} \, . \end{equation} Now assume \begin{equation} {\vartheta}'\in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),2^{N+2}). \end{equation} By the doubling property \eqref{firstdb}, applied five times, we have \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} We have by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} \begin{equation} {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p})\in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})\, . \end{equation} Hence by the triangle inequality \begin{equation} B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')}) \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}'),8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})\, . \end{equation} Together with \eqref{ageo1} and monotonicity \eqref{monotonedb} of $d$ \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{5a+N+2}\, . \end{equation} Using the doubling property \eqref{seconddb} $5a+2$ times gives \begin{equation} d_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}),2^{2-5a^2-2a}D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} Using ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ and $a\ge 4$ gives \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N}\, . \end{equation} With the triangle inequality and \eqref{eqdistqpqp}, \begin{equation} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),{\vartheta}') < 2^{N+2}\, . \end{equation} This shows \begin{equation} B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'),2^{N+2})\subset B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}),2^{N+2})\, . \end{equation} This implies \eqref{lp'lp''} and completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: stack density
nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta} \in {\Theta}$, $N\ge 0$ and $L\in \mathcal{D}$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}:{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G)\le 2^{a(N+5)}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: stack-density

nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta},N,L$ be given and set \begin{equation} \mathfrak{A}':=\{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}:{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})=L\}\, . \end{equation} Let ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$. We have by Definition \eqref{definedens1} using $\lambda=2$ and the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} \begin{equation} \mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G)\le \mu(E_2(2, {\mathfrak p}))\le 2^{a}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}')\mu(L)\, . \end{equation} By the covering property \eqref{thirddb}, applied $N+4$ times, there is a collection ${\Theta}'$ of at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements such that \begin{equation} B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}, 2^{N+1})\subset \bigcup_{{\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'} B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)\, . \end{equation} As each ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')$ with ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ is contained in the left-hand-side of \eqref{eqanti-4} by definition (because ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}))$, it is in at least one $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)$ with ${\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'$. For two different ${\mathfrak p}',{\mathfrak p}''\in \mathfrak{A}'$, we have by \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} that ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$ and ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}'')$ are disjoint and thus by the squeezing property \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball} we have for every ${\vartheta}'\in {\Theta}'$ \begin{equation} {\vartheta}'\not\in B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 0.2)\cap B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}''), 0.2)\, . \end{equation} Hence at most one of ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}')$ and ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'')$ is in $B_{{\mathfrak p}}({\vartheta}', 0.2)$. It follows that there are at most $2^{a(N+4)}$ elements in $\mathfrak{A}'$. Adding \eqref{eqanti-3} over $\mathfrak{A}'$ proves \eqref{eqanti-1}.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: local antichain density
nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta}\in{\Theta}$ and {$N$} be an integer. Let ${\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}$ be a tile with ${\vartheta}\in B_{{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}), 2^{N+1})$. Then we have \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}: {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})) \le \mu (E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: local-antichain-density

nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak p}$ be any tile in $\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$. By definition of $E$, the tile contributes zero to the sum on the left-hand side of \eqref{eqanti-0.5} unless ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}) \neq \emptyset$, which we may assume. With ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})<{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})$ and the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we conclude ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. We conclude from ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ that \begin{equation} {\vartheta} \in B_{\mathfrak p}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), 2^{N+1})\, . \end{equation} With \Cref{tile-reach} and the assumption on ${\mathfrak p}_{\vartheta}$, we conclude \begin{equation} 2^{N+3}{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}} \lesssim 2^{N+3}{\mathfrak p} \, . \end{equation} By Definition \eqref{definee2} of $E_2$, we conclude \begin{equation} E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}}) \subset E_2(2^{N+3},{\mathfrak p}_{{\vartheta}})\, . \end{equation} Using disjointedness of the various $E({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness}, we obtain \eqref{eqanti-0.5}. This proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: global antichain density
nodes.statement: Let ${\vartheta}\in Q(X)$ and let $N\ge 0$ be an integer. Then we have \begin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) \le 2^{101a^3+Na}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}\right)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition
nodes.label: global-antichain-density

nodes.statement:
{Fix ${\vartheta}$ and $N$. Let $\mathfrak{A}'$ be the set of ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$ is not empty and $s({\mathfrak p}) > -S$. Let $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$ be the set of ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$ is not empty and $s({\mathfrak p}) = -S$ } Then we have  egin{equation*} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) = \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) + \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) \end{equation*} We start by estimating the contribution of $\mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. Let $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ with ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}_{-S}$. They all have scale $-S$, by definition of $\mathcal{L}_{-S}$, and hence they are pairwise disjoint by the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty}. We write \[ \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) = \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{-S}, {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = L} \mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G), \] and using \Cref{stack-density}, we estimate  egin{equation} \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{-S}} \mu(L) \le 2^{a(N+5)} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A}) \mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}I_{{\mathfrak p}}ight). \end{equation} We turn to $\mathfrak{A}'$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the collection of dyadic cubes $I\in\mathcal{D}$ such that $I \le {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ for some ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$ and such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})
ot \subset I$ for all ${\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, for each ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'$ and each $x\in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\cap G$, there is $I\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(I)=-S$ and $x\in I$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Since for all ${\mathfrak p}' \in \mathfrak{A}'$ we have $s({\mathfrak p}') > -S$, we have $I \in \mathcal{L}$. Hence  egin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\subset  igcup\{I\in \mathcal{D}: s(I)=-S, I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\}\subset  igcup \mathcal{L}\, . \end{equation} As each $I\in \mathcal{L}$ satisfies $I\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ for some ${\mathfrak p}$ in $\mathfrak{A'}$, we conclude  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}= igcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, . \end{equation} Let $\mathcal{L}^*$ be the set of maximal elements in $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to set inclusion. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the elements in $\mathcal{L}^*$ are pairwise disjoint and we have  egin{equation}  igcup\mathcal{L}^*= igcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{A}'}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\, . \end{equation} Using the partition \eqref{eqdecAprime} into elements of $\mathcal{L}$ in \eqref{eqanti0}, it suffices to show for each $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$  egin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}'}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G \cap L) \le 2^{101a^3+aN} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu(L)\,. \end{equation} Fix $L\in \mathcal{L}^*$. By definition of $\mathcal{L}^*$, there exists an element ${\mathfrak p}'\in \mathfrak{A}'$ such that $L\subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')$. Pick such an element ${\mathfrak p}'$ in $\mathfrak{A}$ with minimal ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. As ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}')
ot \subset L$ by definition of $L$, we have with \eqref{dyadicproperty} that $s(L)< {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}')$. In particular $s(L)<S$, thus $L 
e I_0$ and hence by \eqref{subsetmaxcube} there exists a cube $J \in \mathcal{D}$ with $L \subsetneq J$. By \eqref{coverdyadic}, there is an $L'\in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(L')=s(L)+1$ and $L \le L'$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty}, we have $L\subset L'$. We split the left-hand side of \eqref{eqanti0} as  egin{equation} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.statement: Using that $\mathfrak{A}$ is the disjoint union of the $\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}$ with $N\ge 0$, we estimate the left-hand side \eqref{eq-antichain-Lp} with the triangle inequality by \begin{equation} \le \sum_{N\ge 0} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_G\right\|_{p} \end{equation} We consider each individual term in this sum and estimate its $p$-th power. Using that for each $x\in X$ by \Cref{tile-disjointness} there is at most one ${\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}$ with $x\in E({\mathfrak p})$, we have \begin{equation} \left\|\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}} 2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_G\right\|_{p}^p \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\Big(\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}2^{-N/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})\cap G}(x)\Big)^p\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} =\int\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)}\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})\cap G}(x)\, d\mu(x) \end{equation} \begin{equation} = 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}_{{\vartheta},N}}\mu(E({\mathfrak p})\cap G) \end{equation} Using \Cref{global-antichain-density}, we estimate the last display by \begin{equation} \le 2^{-pN/(2a^2+a^3)+101a^3+Na}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right) \end{equation} Using that $a\ge 4$ and since $p = 4a^4$, we have $$ pN/(2a^2+a^3)\ge 4a^4N/(3a^3) \ge Na+N\, . $$ Hence we have for \eqref{eqanti21} the upper bound $$ \le 2^{101a^3-N}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)\, . $$ Taking the $p$-th root and summing over $N\ge 0$ gives for \eqref{eqanti23} the upper bound $$ \le \left(\sum_{N\ge 0} 2^{-N/p}\right)2^{101a^3/p}\operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{{\frac{1}{p}}}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)^{{\frac{1}{p}}} $$ $$ = \left(1-2^{-1/p}\right)^{-1} 2^{101a^3/p} \operatorname{dens}_1(\mathfrak{A})^{\frac 1p}\mu\left(\cup_{{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak{A}}{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})\right)^{\frac 1p}\, . $$ Using that $p = 4a^4$ and $a \ge 4$, this proves the lemma.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of the Antichain Operator Proposition

nodes.name: convex scales
nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, we have $$ \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x) = \mathbb{Z} \cap [\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x), \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)]\,. $$
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: convex-scales

nodes.statement: Let $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $\underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x) \le s \le \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition of $\sigma$, there exists ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = \underline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$, and there exists ${\mathfrak p}'' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}'') = \overline{\sigma} ({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$. By property \eqref{coverdyadic} of the dyadic grid, there exists a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ of scale $s$ with $x \in I$. By property \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover}, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}(I)$ with ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$. By the dyadic property \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}'')$, and by \eqref{eq-freq-dyadic}, we have ${\Omega}({\mathfrak p}'') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\Omega}({\mathfrak p})$. Thus ${\mathfrak p} \le {\mathfrak p}' \le{\mathfrak p}''$, which gives with the convexity property \eqref{forest2} of ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ that ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, so $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: dyadic partitions
nodes.statement: For each $\mathfrak{S} \subset {\mathfrak P}$, we have \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})}} J \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I = \dot{\bigcup_{L \in \mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})}} L\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: dyadic-partitions

nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ is the set of inclusion maximal cubes in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$, cubes in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ are pairwise disjoint by \eqref{dyadicproperty}. The same applies to $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{S})$. If $x \in \bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, then there exists by \eqref{coverdyadic} a cube $I \in \mathcal{D}$ with $x \in I$ and $s(I) = -S$. Then $I \in \mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$. There exists an inclusion maximal cube in $\mathcal{J}_0(\mathfrak{S})$ containing $I$. This cube contains $x$ and is contained in $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$. This shows one inclusion in \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the other one follows from $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S}) \subset \mathcal{D}$. The proof of the two inclusions in \eqref{eq-L-partition} is similar.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: pointwise tree estimate
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Let $x, x' \in L$. Then for all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support $$ \left|\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x)\right| $$ \begin{equation} \leq 2^{129a^3}(M_{\mathcal{B},1}+S_{1,{\mathfrak u}})P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')+|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}f(x')|, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: pointwise-tree-estimate

nodes.statement: By \eqref{definetp}, if $T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x) \ne 0$, then $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Combining this with $|e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x))| = 1$, we obtain $$ |\sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}[ e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f](x)| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{multline*} Using the triangle inequality, we bound this by the sum of three terms: \begin{multline} \le \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int (e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y) + {Q}(x)(y) + {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x) -{Q}(x)(x))-1)\times\\ K_s(x,y)f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{multline} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. \end{equation} The proof is completed using the bounds for these three terms proven respectively in \Cref{first-tree-pointwise}, \Cref{second-tree-pointwise} and \Cref{third-tree-pointwise}.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: first tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 10 \cdot 2^{104a^3} M_{\mathcal{B}, 1}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. $$
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: first-tree-pointwise

nodes.statement:
Let $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u},x)$. If $x, y \in X$ are such that $K_s(x,y)
eq 0$, then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, we have $ho(x,y)\leq 1/2 D^s$. By $1$-Lipschitz continuity of the function $t \mapsto \exp(it) = e(t)$ and the property \eqref{osccontrol} of the metrics $d_B$, it follows that  egin{multline*} |e(-{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(y)+{Q}(x)(y)+{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})(x)-{Q}(x)(x))-1|\ \leq d_{B(x, 1/2 D^{s})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x))\,. \end{multline*} Let ${\mathfrak p}_s \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}_s) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s)$, and let ${\mathfrak p}'$ be a tile with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$. Using the monotonicity property \eqref{monotonedb}, the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} repeatedly, the definition of $d_{{\mathfrak p}}$ and \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics}, we can bound the previous display by $$ d_{B(x, 4 D^{s})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \leq 2^{4a} d_{{\mathfrak p}_s}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x))\,. $$ Since ${\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}) \in B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 4)$ by \eqref{forest1} and ${Q}(x) \in \Omega({\mathfrak p}') \subset B_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), 1)$ by \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, this is estimated by $$ \le 5 \cdot 2^{4a} 2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)} \,. $$ Using \eqref{eq-Ks-size}, it follows that $$ \eqref{eq-term-A} \le 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B(x,0.5D^{s})}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-J-partition}, the collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $ igcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this is estimated by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\sum_{\substack{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J \cap B(x, 0.5D^s) 
e \emptyset} }\int_{J}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ This expression does not change if we replace $|f|$ by $P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|$. Let $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with $B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. By the triangle inequality and since $x \in E({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4D^{s})$, it follows that $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. Thus we always have $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16 D^s)$. Thus we can continue our chain of estimates with $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B(x,D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16 D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ We have $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \subset B(x, 32D^s)$, by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, since $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}_s)$. Combining this with the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we obtain $$ \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 16D^s)) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^s))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$, it follows that \eqref{eq-term-A} is bounded by $$ 5\cdot 2^{103a^3} \sum_{s\in\sigma(x)}2^{s - \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)}  rac{1}{\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s))}\int_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s),16D^s)}P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f(y)|\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Sinc
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: second tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have $$ \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \le T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(x')\,. $$
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: second-tree-pointwise

nodes.statement: Let $s_1 = \underline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$. By definition, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s_1$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap L$. By \eqref{dyadicproperty} and the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, it follows that $L \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, in particular $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so $x \in I_{s_1}(x')$. Next, let $s_2 = \overline{\sigma}({\mathfrak u}, x)$ and let ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}') = s_2$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p}')$. Since ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have $4{\mathfrak p}' \lesssim {\mathfrak u}$. Since ${Q}(x) \in {\Omega}({\mathfrak p}')$, it follows that $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5\,. $$ Applying the doubling property \eqref{firstdb} five times, we obtain $$ d_{B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have $B(x, D^{s_2}) \subset B(c({\mathfrak p}), 8 D^{s_2})$, so by \eqref{monotonedb} $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{5a}\,. $$ Finally, by applying \eqref{seconddb} $100a$ times, we obtain $$ d_{B(x, D^{s_2-1})}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), {Q}(x)) \le 5 \cdot 2^{-95a} < 1\,. $$ Consequently, $D^{s_2 - 1} < R_Q({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}), x)$. The lemma now follows from the definition of $T_{\mathcal{N}}$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: third tree pointwise
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$, all $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$, all $x, x' \in L$ and all bounded $f$ with bounded support, we have \begin{equation*} \Bigg| \sum_{s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)} \int K_s(x,y) (f(y) - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} f(y)) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \le 2^{128a^3} S_{1,{\mathfrak u}} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: third-tree-pointwise

nodes.statement:
We have for $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$: $$ \int_J K_{s}(x,y)(1 - P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))})f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$  egin{equation} = \int_J  rac{1}{\mu(J)} \int_J K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(z) \,f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} By \eqref{eq-Ks-smooth} and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have for $y, z \in J$ $$ |K_s(x,y) - K_s(x,z)| \le  rac{2^{127a^3}}{\mu(B(x, D^s))} \left( rac{8 D^{s(J)}}{D^s}ight)^{1/a}\,. $$ Suppose that $s \in \sigma({\mathfrak u}, x)$. If $K_s(x,y) 
e 0$ for some $y \in J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ then, by \eqref{supp-Ks}, $y \in B(x, 0.5 D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$. Let ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ with ${\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}) = s$ and $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$. Then $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}_s), 4.5D^s) \cap J 
e \emptyset$ by the triangle inequality. If $s(J) \ge s$ and $s(J) > -S$, then it follows from the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \eqref{defineD} that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 100 D^{s(J)+1})$, contradicting $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Thus $s(J) \le s - 1$ or $s(J) = -S$. If $s(J) = -S$ and $s(J) > s - 1$, then $s = -S$. So in both cases, $s(J) \le s$. It then follows from the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} that $J \subset B(x, 16 D^s)$. Thus, we can estimate \eqref{eq-term-C} by $$ 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}} rac{ m{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x,D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\ s(J) \le {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}} D^{(s(J) - {\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p}))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ $$ = 2^{127a^3 + 3/a}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{\substack{{\mathfrak p}\in \mathfrak{T}\ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I}} rac{ m{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)}{\mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f|\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-dis-freq-cover} and \eqref{defineep}, the sets $E({\mathfrak p})$ for tiles ${\mathfrak p}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = I$ are pairwise disjoint. It follows from the definition of $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ that $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ if and only if $x' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, thus we can estimate the sum over $ m{\mathrm{1}}_{E({\mathfrak p})}(x)$ by $ m{\mathrm{1}}_{I}(x')$. If $x \in E({\mathfrak p})$ then in particular $x \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$, so by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} $B(c(I),16D^{s(I)}) \subset B(x, 32D^{s(I)})$. By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ \mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})) \le 2^{5a} \mu(B(x, D^{s(I)}))\,. $$ Since $a \ge 4$ we can continue our estimate with $$ \le 2^{128a^3}\sum_{I \in \mathcal{D}}  rac{ m{\mathrm{1}}_{I}(x')}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))}\sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\J\subset B(x, 16 D^{s(I)})\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J) - s(I))/a} \int_J |f| $$ $$ = 2^{128a^3} S_{1,{\mathfrak u}} P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x')\,. $$ This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: tree projection estimate
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$. Then we have for all $f, g$ bounded with bounded support $$ \Bigg|\int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} \bar g(y) T_{{\mathfrak p}}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_{2}\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: tree-projection-estimate

nodes.name: nontangential operator bound
nodes.statement: For all bounded $f$ with bounded support and all ${\vartheta} \in {\Theta}$ $$ \|T_{\mathcal{N}}^{{\vartheta}} f\|_2 \le 2^{102a^3} \|f\|_2\,. $$
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: nontangential-operator-bound

nodes.name: boundary operator bound
nodes.statement: For all ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and all bounded functions $f$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \|S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f\|_2 \le 2^{12a} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: boundary-operator-bound

nodes.statement: Let $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$. Let $b(x')$ denote the right-hand side of \Cref{pointwise-tree-estimate}. Apply this lemma to $e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) f$, to obtain for all $y, x' \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le b(x'). $$ Hence, by taking an infimum, we have for $y \in L$ $$ \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \le \inf_{x' \in L} b(x'). $$ Integrating this estimate yields $$ \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L |g(y)| \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times \inf_{x' \in L} b(x') \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ \le \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ By \eqref{definetp}, we have $T_{{\mathfrak p}} f = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f$ for all ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, so $$ \Bigg| \int \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| = \Bigg| \int_{\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} \bar g(y) \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg|\,. $$ Since $\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ partitions $\bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, we get from the triangle inequality $$ \le \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L |g(y)| \Bigg| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f(y) \Bigg| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ which by the above computation is bounded by $$ \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_L P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ $$ = \int_X P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|(y) \times b(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) $$ Applying Cauchy-Schwarz, this is bounded by $\|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|g|\|_2 \times \|b\|_2$. By Minkowski's inequality, \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, \Cref{nontangential-operator-bound} and \Cref{boundary-operator-bound}, $\|b\|_2$ is at most $$ 2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a})\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 + 2^{103a^3} \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]\|_2\,. $$ By the triangle inequality we have for all $x \in X$ that $|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}[e({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}))f]|(x) \le P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|(x)$, thus we can further estimate the above by $$ (2^{129a^3} (2^{2a+1} + 2^{12a}) + 2^{103a^3}) \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2\,. $$ This completes the proof since $a \ge 4$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.statement: Fix $s_1, s_2$. By \eqref{eq-psisum} we have for all $x \in (0, \infty)$ $$ \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1 - \sum_{s < s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x) - \sum_{s > s_1} \psi(D^{-s}x)\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, the two sums on the right hand side are zero for all $x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2 - 1}]$, hence $$ x \in [\frac{1}{2}D^{s_1-1}, \frac{1}{4} D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1\,. $$ Since $\psi$ is supported in $[\frac{1}{4D}, \frac{1}{2}]$, we further have $$ x \notin [\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}, \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}] \implies \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 0\,. $$ Finally, since $\psi \ge 0$ and $\sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}} \psi(D^{-s}x) = 1$, we have for all $x$ $$ 0 \le \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}x) \le 1\,. $$ Let $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and suppose that $D^{s_2 - 1} \le R_Q({\vartheta}, x')$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, it holds that $\rho(x,x') \le 8D^{s_1}$. We have $$ \Bigg|\sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \int K_s(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ $$ = \Bigg|\int \sum_{s = s_1}^{s_2} \psi(D^{-s}\rho(x',y)) K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{equation} \le \Bigg| \int_{8D^{s_1} < \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \Bigg| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_1-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le 8D^{s_1}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \int_{\frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1} \le \rho(x',y) \le \frac{1}{2}D^{s_2}} |K(x', y)| |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{equation} The first term \eqref{eq-sharp-trunc-term} is at most $2T_{{Q}}^{\vartheta} f(x)$, using with $R_1 := 8D^{s_1}$, $R_2 := \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ and $R_1 < R_2 < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')$ the triangle inequality in the form \begin{equation} \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) \le R_2} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le \left|\int_{R_1 < \rho(x',y) < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} + \left|\int_{R_2 < \rho(x',y) < R_{{Q}}({\vartheta},x')} K(x',y) f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right|. \end{equation} The other two terms will be estimated by the finitary maximal function from \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}. For the second term \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} we use \eqref{eqkernel-size} which implies that for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}$, we have $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_1 - 1}))}\,. $$ Using $D=2^{100a^2}$ and the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 +100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a+101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32D^{s_1}))}\, . \end{equation} By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_1}) \subset B(c(I_{s_1}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_1}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_1})\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{pf-nontangential-operator-bound-imeq}, we conclude that \eqref{eq-lower-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a + 101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ For \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} we argue similarly. We have for all $y$ with $\rho(x', y) \ge \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}$ $$ |K(x', y)| \le \frac{2^{a^3}}{\mu(B(x', \frac{1}{4}D^{s_2-1}))}\,. $$ Using the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $7 + 100a^2$ times estimates the last display by \begin{equation} \le \frac{2^{7a + 101a^3}}{\mu(B(x', 32 D^{s_2}))}\, . \end{equation} Note that by \eqref{dyadicproperty} we have $I_{s_1}(x) \subset I_{s_2}(x)$, in particular $x' \in I_{s_2}(x)$. By the triangle inequality and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we have $$ B(x', 8D^{s_2}) \subset B(c(I_{s_2}(x)), 16D^{s(I_{s_2}(x))}) \subset B(x', 32D^{s_2})\,. $$ Combining this, \eqref{eq-upper-bound-term} is at most $$ 2^{7a+101a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x)\,. $$ Using $a \ge 4$, taking a supremum over all $x' \in I_{s_1}(x)$ and then a supremum over all $-S \le s_1 < s_2 \le S$, we obtain $$ T_{\mathcal{N}} f(x) \le 2T_{{Q}}^{\vartheta} f(x) + 2^{102a^3} M_{\mathcal{B},1} f(x

Suppose that $B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e \emptyset$ and $s(I) = s(J)$. Then $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}) \subset B(c(J), 128 D^{s(J)})$. Hence by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx} $$ 2^{9a}\mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})) \ge \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,, $$ and by the triangle inequality, $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)})$ is contained in $B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is any finite collection of cubes $J \in \mathcal{D}$ satisfying $s(J) = s(I)$ and  egin{equation*} B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}) \cap B(c(J), 16 D^{s(J)}) 
e\emptyset\ , \end{equation*} then it follows from \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and pairwise disjointedness of cubes of the same scale \eqref{dyadicproperty} that the balls $B(c(J),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J)})$ are pairwise disjoint. Hence  egin{align*} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)})) &\ge \sum_{J \in \mathcal{C}} \mu(B(c(J),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J)}))\ &\ge |\mathcal{C}| 2^{-9a} \mu(B(c(I), 33 D^{s(I)}))\,. \end{align*} Since $\mu$ is doubling and $\mu

nodes.statement: Note that by definition, $S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ is a finite sum of indicator functions of cubes $I \in \mathcal{D}$ for each locally integrable $f$, and hence is bounded, has bounded support and is integrable. Let $g$ be another function with the same three properties. Then $\bar g S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ is integrable, and we have $$ \Bigg|\int \bar g(y) S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| $$ \begin{multline*} = \Bigg|\sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)}))} \int_I \bar g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\s(J)\le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\Bigg| \end{multline*} \begin{multline*} \le \sum_{I\in\mathcal{D}} \frac{1}{\mu(B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)}))} \int_{B(c(I), 16D^{s(I)})} | g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\\ \times \sum_{\substack{J\in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\,:\,J\subseteq B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(J) \le s(I)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}\int_J |f(y)| \,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. \end{multline*} Changing the order of summation and using $J \subset B(c(I), 16 D^{s(I)})$ to bound the first average integral by $M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y)$ for any $y \in J$, we obtain \begin{align} \le \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \sum_{\substack{I \in \mathcal{D} \, : \, J\subset B(c(I),16 D^{s(I)})\\ s(I) \ge s(J)}} D^{(s(J)-s(I))/a}. \end{align} By \Cref{boundary-overlap}, there are at most $2^{9a}$ cubes $I$ at each scale satisfying the inclusion $J \subset B(c(I),16D^{s(I)})$. Since $D^{-1/a}\le\frac12$, $(1 - D^{-1/a})^{-1} \le 2$. Using this estimate for the sum of the geometric series, we conclude that \eqref{eq-boundary-operator-bound-1} is at most $$ 2^{9a+1} \sum_{J\in\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}\int_J|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ The collection $\mathcal{J}$ is a partition of $\bigcup_{I \in \mathcal{D}} I$, so this equals $$ 2^{9a+1} \int_X|f(y)| M_{\mathcal{B},1}|g|(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ Using Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{Hardy-Littlewood}, we conclude $$ \left|\int \bar g S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| \le 2^{12a} \|g\|_2\|f\|_2\,. $$ The lemma now follows by choosing $g = S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f$ and dividing on both sides by the finite $\|S_{1,{\mathfrak u}}f\|_2$.

nodes.statement: Denote $$ \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u}) = \bigcup_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} E({\mathfrak p})\,. $$ Then we have $$ \left| \int_X \bar g \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{ g\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} (\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})}f) \, \mathrm{d}\mu \right|\,. $$ By \Cref{tree-projection-estimate}, this is bounded by \begin{equation} \le 2^{130a^3}\|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} |\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}g|\|_2\,. \end{equation} We bound the two factors separately. We have $$ \|P_{\mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} |\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{\mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})}g|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(L)} \left(\int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})} |g(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz and \Cref{local-dens1-tree-bound} this is at most $$ \le \left( \sum_{L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} 2^{101a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \int_{L \cap \mathcal{E}({\mathfrak u})} |g(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes $L \in \mathcal{L}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is \begin{equation} \le 2^{51 a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. \end{equation} Similarly, we have \begin{equation} \|P_{\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))}|f|\|_2 = \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. \end{equation} By Cauchy-Schwarz, this is $$ \le \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \int_J |f(y)|^2 \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y) \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ Since cubes in $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ are pairwise disjoint by \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, this is at most \begin{equation} \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Combining \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree}, \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-J-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est}. If $f \le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F$ then $f = f\bm{\mathrm{1}}_F$, so $$ \left( \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_J |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2} $$ $$ =\left(\sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))} \frac{1}{\mu(J)} \left(\int_{J \cap F} |f(y)| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\right)^2 \right)^{1/2}\,. $$ We estimate as before, using now \Cref{local-dens2-tree-bound} and Cauchy-Schwarz, and obtain that this is $$ \le 2^{101a^3} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|f\|_2\,. $$ Combining this with \eqref{eq-both-factors-tree} and \eqref{eq-factor-L-tree} gives \eqref{eq-cor-tree-est-F}.

It suffices to show that there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak P}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') = L'$, $d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u})) < 4$ and $9{\mathfrak p}'' \lesssim 9{\mathfrak p}'$. If $q \in B_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), 1)$, then by a similar calculation as above, using the triangle inequality, \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and \eqref{forest1}, we obtain $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), q) \le d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}'), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q})) + d_{{\mathfrak q}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak q}), q) \le 9\,. $$ Thus $L \cap G \cap E({\mathfrak q}) \subset E_2(9, {\mathfrak p}')$. nodes.statement: We prove the inequality with the constant $2^{201a^3}$ replaced by $2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a}$; this is stronger because $a \geq 4$. It suffices to show the existence of a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ and an $r \geq 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$ such that $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)$ and $\mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) ≤ 2 ^ {200a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)$, because then it follows from the definition \eqref{definedens2} of $\operatorname{dens}_2$ that $$ \mu(F \cap J) \le \mu(F \cap B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) $$ $$ \le \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), r)) \le 2^{200a^3 + 14a} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))\mu(J)\,. $$ In particular, these criteria are satisfied, with $r = 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$, by any ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ such that $J \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}, 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))$ and $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$, because then by the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $$ \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})) \le 2^{4a} \mu(B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})} / 4)) $$ $$ \le 2^{4a} \mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 14a} \mu(J)\,. $$ Suppose first that $s(J) = S$. Then $J = I_0$, so \eqref{subsetmaxcube} and the fact that $J \in \mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})) \subseteq \mathcal{J}_0({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ imply that $s(J) = -S$. Thus $S = 0$. It follows that $J$ is the only dyadic cube, so any ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ has ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) = J$, and therefore satisfies $J \subseteq B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}, 4 D ^ {{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}))$ and $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. It remains to consider the case $s(J) < S$. Then, by \eqref{coverdyadic} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, there exists some cube $J' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $J \subset J'$. By definition of $\mathcal{J}({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))$ there exists some ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$ such that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$. Since $c(J) \in J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')})$, the triangle inequality, $s(J') = s(J) + 1$ and $D=2^{100a^2}$ imply $$ B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J')+1}) \subset B(c(J), 204D^{s(J') + 1} + 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B(c(J), 2^8 D^{s(J) + 2})\,. $$ From the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, $D=2^{100a^2}$ and \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube}, we obtain \begin{equation} \mu(B(c(J'), 204D^{s(J') + 1})) \leq 2 ^ {200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,. \end{equation} If $J \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$, then we need only check that $\mu({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})) \le 2^{100a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)$. This follows immediately from ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})$ and \eqref{measure-comparison}. From now on we assume $J \not \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 4 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$. Since \begin{equation*} {\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}) \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J'), 100 D^{s(J') + 1})\, , \end{equation*} we have by \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality $$ J \subset J' \subset B(c(J'), 4D^{s(J')}) \subset B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})\,. $$ In particular this implies $104 D^{s(J') + 1} > 4D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}$. By the triangle inequality we also have $$ B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1}) \subset B(c(J), 204 D^{s(J') + 1})\,, $$ so from \eqref{measure-comparison}, $$ \mu( B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 104 D^{s(J') + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 10a} \mu(J)\,, $$ which proves ${\mathfrak p}$ satisfies the needed criteria with $r=104 D^{s(J') + 1}$.

nodes.statement: For each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak P}$, we have $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g\,. $$ For each ${\mathfrak u} \in {\mathfrak U}$ and each ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})$, we have $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})} g\,. $$

nodes.statement: By \eqref{forest1}, $E({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$. Thus by \eqref{definetp*} $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x) $$ $$ = \int_{E({\mathfrak p})} \overline{K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x)} e(-{Q}(y)(x) + {Q}(y)(y)) \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})}(y) g(y) \, \mathrm{d}\mu(y)\,. $$ If this integral is not $0$, then there exists $y \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$ such that $K_{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}(y,x) \ne 0$. By \eqref{supp-Ks}, \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and the triangle inequality, it follows that \begin{equation*} x \in B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5 D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})\, . \end{equation*} Thus $$ T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g(x) = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})}(x) T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* (\bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})} g)(x)\,. $$ The second claimed equation follows now since ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$ and by \eqref{forest6} we have $B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 5D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u})$.

nodes.statement: For all bounded $g$ supported on $G$ we have that $$ \left\| \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,, $$ $$ \left\| \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g\right\|_2 \le 2^{282a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \operatorname{dens}_2({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2\,. $$

nodes.statement: By \Cref{densities-tree-bound}, we have for all bounded $f$ and $g$ with $|g| \le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_G$ that $$ \left| \int_X \overline{\sum_{{\mathfrak p}\in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| = \left| \int_X \overline{g} \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}} f \,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| $$ \begin{equation} \le 2^{181a^3} \operatorname{dens}_1({\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2\,. \end{equation} Let $f = \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$. Since $|g| \le \bm{\mathrm{1}}_G$, $f$ is bounded and has bounded support. In particular $\|f\|_2 < \infty$. Dividing \eqref{eq-adjoint-bound} by $\|f\|_2$ completes the proof. The proof of the second part is similar with $f = \bm{\mathrm{1}}_F \sum_{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u})} T_{{\mathfrak p}}^* g$.

nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: correlation-separated-trees

nodes.statement: By \Cref{adjoint-tile-support} and \eqref{dyadicproperty}, the left hand side \eqref{eq-lhs-sep-tree} is $0$ unless ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ or ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Without loss of generality we assume that ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. Define \begin{equation} \mathfrak{S} := \{{\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \ : \ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn/2}\,\}. \end{equation} \Cref{correlation-separated-trees} follows by combining the definition \eqref{defineZ} of $Z$ with the following two lemmas.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: correlation distant tree parts
nodes.statement: We have for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \cap \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{511a^3} 2^{-Zn/(4a^2 + 2a^3)} \prod_{j =1}^2 \| S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1))}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: correlation-distant-tree-parts

nodes.name: correlation near tree parts
nodes.statement: We have for all ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ and all bounded $g_1, g_2$ with bounded support \begin{equation} \left| \int_X \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_1 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)} \sum_{{\mathfrak p}_2 \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2) \setminus \mathfrak{S}} T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_1}g_1 \overline{T^*_{{\mathfrak p}_2}g_2 }\,\mathrm{d}\mu \right| \end{equation} \begin{equation} \le 2^{232a^3+21a+5} 2^{-\frac{25}{101a}Zn\kappa} \prod_{j=1}^2 \|S_{2, {\mathfrak u}_j} g_j\|_{L^2({\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1))}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: correlation-near-tree-parts

nodes.name: overlap implies distance
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathfrak u}_1 \ne {\mathfrak u}_2 \in {\mathfrak U}$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \cup {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$ with ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$, then ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. In particular, we have ${\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: overlap-implies-distance

nodes.statement: Suppose first that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_2)$, by \eqref{forest1}. Thus we have by the separation condition \eqref{forest5}, \eqref{eq-freq-comp-ball}, \eqref{forest1} and the triangle inequality \begin{align*} d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) &\ge d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) - d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak p}), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1))\\ &\ge 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4\\ &\ge 2^{Zn/2}\,, \end{align*} using that $Z= 2^{12a}\ge 4$. Hence ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. Suppose now that ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_2)$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, then the same argument as above with ${\mathfrak u}_1$ and ${\mathfrak u}_2$ swapped shows ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$. If ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \not \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ then, by \eqref{dyadicproperty}, ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Pick ${\mathfrak p}' \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1)$, we have ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}') \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p})$. Hence, by \Cref{monotone-cube-metrics} and the first paragraph $$ d_{{\mathfrak p}}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge d_{{\mathfrak p}'}({\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_1), {\mathcal{Q}}({\mathfrak u}_2)) \ge 2^{Zn}\,, $$ so ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: dyadic partition 1
nodes.statement: We have that $$ {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) = \dot{\bigcup_{J \in \mathcal{J}'}} J\,. $$
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: dyadic-partition-1

nodes.statement: By \Cref{dyadic-partitions}, it remains only to show that each $J \in \mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$ with $J \cap {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \ne \emptyset$ is in $\mathcal{J}'$. But if $J \notin \mathcal{J}'$, then by \eqref{dyadicproperty} ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset J$. Pick ${\mathfrak p} \in {\mathfrak T}({\mathfrak u}_1) \subset \mathfrak{S}$. Then ${\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset J$. This contradicts the definition of $\mathcal{J}(\mathfrak{S})$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition

nodes.name: Lipschitz partition unity
nodes.statement: There exists a family of functions $\chi_J$, $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ such that \begin{equation} \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)} = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} \chi_J\,, \end{equation} and for all $J \in \mathcal{J}'$ and all $y,y' \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$ \begin{equation} 0 \leq \chi_J(y) \leq \bm{\mathrm{1}}_{B(J)}(y)\,, \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le 2^{227a^3} \frac{\rho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}}\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: Lipschitz-partition-unity

nodes.name: moderate scale change
nodes.statement: If $J, J' \in \mathcal{J'}$ with $$ B(J) \cap B(J') \ne \emptyset\,, $$ then $|s(J) - s(J')| \le 1$.
nodes.section: 7 Proof of the Forest Operator Proposition
nodes.label: moderate-scale-change

nodes.statement:
For each cube $J \in \mathcal{J}$ let $$ 	ilde\chi_J(y) =  m{\mathrm{1}}_{{\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)}(y)\max\{0, 8 - D^{-s(J)} ho(y, c(J))\}\,, $$ and set $$ a(y) = \sum_{J \in \mathcal{J}'} 	ilde \chi_J(y)\,. $$ We define \[ \chi_J(y) :=  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y)}{a(y)}\,. \] Then, due to \eqref{forest6} and \eqref{def-BJ}, the properties \eqref{eq-pao-1} and \eqref{eq-pao-2} are clearly true. Estimate \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows from \eqref{eq-pao-2} if $y, y' 
otin B(J)$. Thus we can assume that $y \in B(J)$. We have by the triangle inequality $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le  rac{|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')|}{a(y)} +  rac{	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|}{a(y)a(y')} $$ Since $	ilde \chi_J(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in B(c(J),4D^{s(J)}) \supset J$ and by \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, we have that $a(z) \ge 4$ for all $z \in {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak u}_1)$. So we can estimate the above further by $$ \le 2^{-2}(|	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 	ilde \chi_J(y')|a(y) - a(y')|)\,. $$ If $y' 
otin B({\mathrm{c}}({\mathfrak p}), 8D^{{\mathrm{s}}({\mathfrak p})})$ then the second summand vanishes. Else, we can estimate the above, using also that $|	ilde \chi_J(y')| \le 8$, by $$ \le 2^{-2} |	ilde \chi_J(y) - 	ilde \chi_J(y')| + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}}|	ilde \chi_{J'}(y) - 	ilde \chi_{J'} (y')|\,. $$ By the triangle inequality, we have for all dyadic cubes $I$ $$ |	ilde \chi_I(y) - 	ilde \chi_I(y')| \le ho(y, y') D^{-s(I)}\,. $$ Using this above, we obtain $$ |\chi_J(y) - \chi_J(y')| \le ho(y,y') \Big(  rac{1}{4} D^{-s(J)} + 2 \sum_{\substack{J' \in \mathcal{J}'\ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset}} D^{-s(J')}\Big)\,. $$ By \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, this is at most $$  rac{ho(y,y')}{D^{s(J)}} \left(  rac{1}{4} + 2D |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J) 
e \emptyset\}|ight)\,. $$ By \eqref{eq-vol-sp-cube} and \Cref{dyadic-partition-1}, the balls $B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4} D^{s(J')})$ are pairwise disjoint. By the triangle inequality and \Cref{moderate-scale-change}, each such ball for $J'$ in the set of the last display is contained in $$ B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})\,. $$ By the doubling property \eqref{doublingx}, we further have $$ \mu(B(c(J), 9 D^{s(J) + 1})) \le 2^{200a^3 + 7a} \mu\Big(B(c(J'),  rac{1}{4}D^{s(J')})\Big) $$ for each such ball. Thus $$ |\{J' \in \mathcal{J}' \ : \ B(J') \cap B(J)

e \emptyset\}|\leq 2^{200a^3 + 100a^2 + 7a + 2}.$$ Since $a\ge 4$, \eqref{eq-pao-3} follows.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $s(J') < s(J) - 1$. Then $s(J) > -S$. Thus, by the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$ there exists no ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,. \end{equation} Since $s(J') < s(J)$, there exists a cube $J'' \in \mathcal{D}$ with $J \subset J''$ and $s(J'') = s(J') + 1$. By the definition of $\mathcal{J}'$, there exists a tile ${\mathfrak p} \in \mathfrak{S}$ with \begin{equation} {\mathcal{I}}({\mathfrak p}) \subset B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2})\,. \end{equation} But by the triangle inequality and \eqref{defineD}, we have $$ B(c(J''), 100 D^{s(J')+2}) \subset B(c(J), 100D^{s(J) + 1})\,, $$ which contradicts \eqref{eq-tile-incl-1} and \eqref{tile-incl-2}.
